description: Family 7: Sam & Alex — two parents, both 21+, one earning above threshold, one not working. Not on Universal Credit. One child (Freddie, age 1) with a childminder. Tests: non-working partner disqualifies family from ALL work-tested schemes. This is the starkest 'no government support' scenario — despite one parent being in full-time paid work, the non-working partner creates a complete gap in childcare support.

costEstimate.description: Worked example for Sam & Alex. Sam is working full-time and earning above the £195/week threshold. Alex is not working. In a two-parent household, BOTH parents must meet the work test. Because Alex is not working, the family fails the both-parents-working test and receives zero government support.

freddie.narrative: Freddie attends Lisa Henderson's childminding service (provider_24) for 30 hours per week over 44 weeks per year. At age 1, Freddie is over the 9-month threshold that would normally make him eligible for funded hours. However, Alex is not working and has no qualifying exception — so Freddie receives no funded hours at all. The childminder charges £5.50/hr for under-2s.

selections.source: provider_24 (Lisa Henderson, under-2 rate: £5.50/hr, 48 operating weeks)
selections.configuration: 30 hours per week, 44 weeks per year

step1_childcareFees.note: Using provider_24 under-2 rate: £5.50/hr. Family uses 44 of the childminder's 48 operating weeks.

step2_fundedHoursReduction.reason: Both parents must be working (or meet specific exceptions). Alex is not working and has no qualifying exception.
step2_fundedHoursReduction.whatIfNote: If Alex were working (earning above £195.36/week), Freddie would gain 15 funded hours per week. At the childminder's rate of £5.50/hr, this would save the parent 15 × £5.50 × 38 = £3,135.00 per year.

step3_taxFreeChildcare.reason: Same both-parents-working test. Alex is not working, so TFC is not available.
step3_taxFreeChildcare.whatIfNote: If Alex were working, the family could receive a 20% top-up capped at £2,000/year per child.

step4_ucChildcare.reason: The family is not on Universal Credit.

meals.note: Freddie attends approximately 6 hours per day (30 hrs / 5 days), qualifying for a daily meal charge.

totalCostOfChildcare.description: The total annual cost of all childcare for this family, before any government support is applied.

fundedHours.note: Freddie is age-eligible for the working parent entitlement (over 9 months, under 2). Sam meets the earnings test. But Alex is not working — so the family is ineligible.

taxFreeChildcare.note: TFC requires both parents to be working. Alex is not working.

ucChildcare.scheme: Not eligible — not on Universal Credit

familyTotal.summaryNote: This is the starkest 'no government support' scenario. Despite one parent working full-time, the non-working partner disqualifies the family from all work-tested schemes. The family pays the full £7,810 with zero government contribution. The lower absolute cost compared to Oxford (£10,560) reflects Sunderland's cheaper childminder rates (£5.50/hr vs £7.50/hr), but the policy outcome is identical: 0% support.

nonWorkingPartnerImpact.description: The financial impact of having a non-working partner rather than a working partner.
nonWorkingPartnerImpact.note: The difference between a non-working partner and a working partner is over £5,000 per year in government support.
